title: Why You Should Consider Shorting Bonds Right Now
speaker: Ted Parkhill (Incline Investment Management), with tastylive hosts

macro_themes.view: Persistent inflation and the first hikes in decades mean rates can keep rising; trend followers remain short bonds broadly.
Bonds are no longer a safe haven; investors need non-correlated returns.
No easy resolution to the Iran war; stays long energy until the trend ends. Host thinks the oil sell-off is fake given backwardation.

calls.reason: Short bonds (= yields up) because of persistent inflation and a rising-rate trend; trend-following positioning.
calls.quote: in general we remain short bonds. Why? Cuz we're in this environment of of rising rates.

calls.reason: Guest stays long energy while the war chops; host sees backwardation and a deferred curve at 80-82 as signs the sell-off isn't done.
calls.quote: our view is we're going to be as long energy until it's over.

calls.reason: No trend in gold now (down ~8% on the year), so the system is flat.
calls.quote: You You go flat. And and for us, being flat is a position.

notes: Date: host says the election is 'in the next 28 days'; US midterms are Tue 2026-11-03, so 28 days before = Tue 2026-10-06 (listing approx_date 2026-10-07). Date derived from that remark, so treat as approximate (±1 day). Bond view is recorded as TNX bullish (yields up) because the guest is short bonds; no specific contract named. Guest repeatedly stresses he makes no predictions (trend follower), so biases reflect current positioning.
